seoTitle: GoDaddy SEO Cost & Is It Worth It in 2026
metaDescription: Thinking about GoDaddy's SEO service? See what it costs, what features it includes, and the pros and cons before deciding if it's worth it for your site.
intro: GoDaddy folds SEO tools into its Website Builder plans rather than selling them as a standalone product, which makes the real cost a little harder to pin down than a single advertised price. This guide walks through where those SEO features actually live in your GoDaddy account, what the paid tier adds over the free one, and what's still missing even once you pay — so you can judge the value against your budget rather than a marketing headline.

steps.heading: Start from your GoDaddy dashboard
steps.body: After logging in, the "Jump back in!" panel on your dashboard shows your active domain and website at a glance, with an "All Products and Services" list underneath covering Domains, hosting, and anything else on the account. This is also where GoDaddy surfaces upgrade prompts for the site tied to that domain, which is the path that leads to the SEO-inclusive plans rather than a dedicated "SEO" menu item anywhere in the account.

image.caption: The GoDaddy dashboard's "Jump back in!" panel, showing an active domain and website with the full product list below it.

steps.heading: Check the Website Builder pricing card
steps.body: Scrolling GoDaddy's own site under "More ways to grow" surfaces the Website Builder pricing card directly, showing a starting price with a note about savings for paying annually versus month-to-month. The number you see here is localized to your account's region and currency, so treat the exact figure as an example rather than a fixed global price — the important thing to check is your own account's displayed rate before assuming a number quoted online applies to you.

image.caption: The Website Builder pricing card, showing a starting monthly price with a discount noted for an annual commitment.

steps.heading: See what the SEO-inclusive plan actually promises
steps.body: Clicking into the upgrade prompt opens a "Get 2X more traffic with SEO" panel listing what's included in the paid Basic plan: tools to help your site rank higher on Google, suggestions for high-value keywords personalized to your site, the ability to connect a custom domain, and removal of GoDaddy's own ads from your free site. None of this is an SEO specialist doing manual work — it's automated suggestions and on-page tooling, which is worth knowing going in so you're not expecting agency-level service for a website-builder add-on price.

image.caption: The "Get 2X more traffic with SEO" upgrade panel, listing keyword suggestions, custom domain support, and ad removal as part of the Basic plan.

steps.heading: Compare the Free and Basic plans side by side
steps.body: GoDaddy's own Compare plans screen lines up the Free tier at $0/mo against Basic at $9.99/mo, and it's worth actually reading the feature rows rather than assuming Basic unlocks everything. In the online store and marketplace section, features like online store products, marketplace selling on Amazon or Etsy, gift cards, and abandoned cart recovery all show as unavailable on both Free and Basic — those live in GoDaddy's higher commerce tiers, not the SEO-focused plan. That distinction matters: Basic buys you SEO tooling and a custom domain, not e-commerce functionality, so don't upgrade expecting store features to come along with it.

image.caption: The Compare plans screen, Free at $0/mo versus Basic at $9.99/mo — note that store and marketplace features stay unavailable on both tiers.

steps.heading: Weigh what you're actually paying for
steps.body: At roughly ten dollars a month (or the equivalent Website Builder price in your currency), GoDaddy's SEO tooling is cheap compared to a dedicated SEO platform or hiring freelance help, but it's also shallow by comparison — you're getting automated keyword suggestions and basic on-page guidance, not backlink building, technical audits, or content strategy. For a brand-new site that just needs its metadata and basic structure in reasonable shape, that's a fair trade. For a site that's already established and needs real competitive movement in rankings, the Basic plan alone won't get you there.

steps.heading: Know when to look beyond GoDaddy
steps.body: If your site's growth depends on outranking real competitors rather than just getting the basics right, budget for a standalone SEO tool or a specialist once GoDaddy's built-in suggestions stop moving the needle. Nothing about upgrading locks you in — like other GoDaddy add-ons, the SEO-inclusive plan can be downgraded or canceled if it isn't delivering, so it's reasonable to start with Basic, see what it actually does for your traffic over a couple of months, and reassess from there rather than committing to a bigger spend up front.

faq.question: Is GoDaddy SEO worth it for a small business?
faq.answer: It's a reasonable, low-cost starting point for a new or small site already on GoDaddy's Website Builder, but it's shallow compared to dedicated SEO tools once your site is established and needs to compete for harder keywords.

faq.question: How does GoDaddy SEO pricing compare to other SEO tools?
faq.answer: GoDaddy's Basic plan runs around $9.99/mo (or the local Website Builder equivalent) and bundles SEO features with hosting, which is far cheaper than standalone SEO platforms — but those platforms typically go much deeper than automated keyword suggestions.

faq.question: Does GoDaddy SEO guarantee better rankings?
faq.answer: No SEO service, including GoDaddy's, can guarantee specific rankings, since search results depend on many factors beyond any one tool's suggestions.

faq.question: What's actually included in GoDaddy's paid SEO plan?
faq.answer: The Basic plan's SEO panel lists tools to help you rank higher on Google, personalized keyword suggestions, custom domain support, and removal of GoDaddy's own ads from your site.

faq.question: Does upgrading for SEO also unlock online store features?
faq.answer: No. GoDaddy's own plan comparison shows online store products, marketplace selling, gift cards, and abandoned cart recovery all unavailable on both the Free and Basic tiers — those require a higher commerce plan.
